chunks: Abu al-Maghra narrated from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked him about a man who committed fornication with a woman and then after that wanted to marry her, so he said: "If she repents, she becomes lawful for him."
I said: "And how is her repentance known?" He said: "He invites her to what they had been upon of the unlawful act; then if she refuses and seeks forgiveness from her Lord, her repentance is known."

key_terms.الْحَرَامِ: the forbidden act they had previously committed
key_terms.تَابَتْ: she repented and turned back from the sin
key_terms.تَوْبَتُهَا: her repentance, as evidenced by her conduct
key_terms.حَلَّتْ لَهُ: she became lawful for him to marry
key_terms.فَجَرَ: committed fornication or an illicit sexual act
key_terms.يَتَزَوَّجَهَا: to marry her in a lawful marriage

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry a woman after committing zina with her if she repents?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning marriage to a woman with whom a man had previously committed zina. It states that marriage becomes lawful if she has truly repented, and it identifies refusal to return to the haram act together with seeking forgiveness as a sign of sincere tawbah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4457 - Abu al-Maghra narrated from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Imam (as) about a man who committed fornication with a woman and then later wanted to marry her.
Imam (as) said: "If she repents, she becomes lawful for him."

I asked: "And how can her repentance be known?"
Imam (as) replied: "He should invite her to engage in the same unlawful act they previously committed. If she refuses and seeks forgiveness from her Lord (azj), then her repentance is known."
